title: GSA Issues Final Rule on Large Language Model Procurements
key_facts: GSA issued clause 552.239-7001, Basic Safeguarding of Data within Large Language Model Artificial Intelligence Systems, on 28 Sep 2026; it takes effect 19 Oct 2026.
A March 2026 draft would have banned AI components 'manufactured, developed, or controlled by non-U.S. entities'; a 17 Jun revision dropped the ban.
The final clause narrows what counts as Government Data and ties flow-down duties to NIST AI Risk Management Framework task categories.
The 72-hour incident notice now applies only to incidents affecting an LLM used in the contract that may affect government data.
The June demands that the model be 'neutral' and free of ideological dogma are replaced by one duty of reasonable efforts to prioritise accuracy, scientific inquiry and objectivity.
The government may suspend use of the LLM at any time; contractor decommissioning liability is capped at 25 percent of the affected order's value.
The clause still overrides contractors' commercial agreements.
quote_evidence: The Final Clause will become effective on October 19, 2026.

However, the Final Clause leaves unchanged the operative rule that the clause overrides all contractor commercial agreements, and industry concerns regarding the order of precedence will likely persist.
why_it_matters_hint: Sets the data-handling and AI-behaviour terms for firms selling large language models to the US government.
notes: Law-firm style analysis of an official clause; one outlet.
